result.output:
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup          Build the brain and start background updates
  add            Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  init-agents    Install coordinated agent instructions
  agent-guide    Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  mcp            Serve local brain tools over MCP stdio
  config         Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview       Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief          Gather relevant context for a task
  query          Search the brain (hybrid by default)
  get            Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get      Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash           Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable facts & patterns:
  recall         Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  remember       Record a durable fact about this repository
  distill        Extract durable facts from sessions (requires an agent)
  facts          Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  verify         Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  patterns       Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Sessions & conversation memory:
  memory         Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  privacy        Control which captured sessions the brain retains

Code & semantic index:
  inspect        Explore code, dependencies, and change history
---QUERY HELP---
Search the brain (hybrid by default). Supply the text positionally or with --query. Flags may appear before or after the text.

Usage:
  entire-brain query [query] [flags]

Flags:
      --after string          Conversation source only: sessions at or after this time (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD)
      --agent string          Conversation source only: exchanges captured by this agent/harness (e.g. "Claude Code", "Codex")
      --before string         Conversation source only: sessions before this time (RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD)
      --branch string         Branch for facts (default: current); with --source conversation also filters exchanges to that captured branch
      --concept stringArray   Conversation source only: additional concept (repeatable, up to 4); sessions must match the query AND every concept
      --format string         Output format: json or cli (QMD-style alias for --json)
  -h, --help                  help for query
      --include-abstract      Conversation source only: include bounded evidence-linked session previews (never affects ranking)
      --json                  Emit machine-readable JSON
      --keyword               Match keywords and identifiers only
      --limit int             Maximum results (default 10)
  -n, --number int            Maximum results (QMD-style alias for --limit) (default 10)
      --patterns              Also surface relevant pattern:/theme: pointers (does not change facts/history/docs ranking)
      --query string          Query text (alternative to the positional query)
      --semantic              Match meaning using vector similarity only
      --session string        Conversation source only: exchanges from this session id (also disables the per-session diversity cap)
      --source string         Restrict retrieval to one source: all, fact, history, conversation, or doc (default all; conversation is experimental opt-in)

result.output:
# Benchmarks

Selected measurements of Brain, their limits, and commands for evaluating your
own repository. Historical results include both gains and closed negatives.

**What this page is not:** a head-to-head against another memory product. We
have not run one under conditions we would defend, and [saying so](#head-to-head-against-other-products)
is more useful than a number nobody can reproduce.

## Run it yourself

You should not have to take our numbers on trust. These two need no
configuration, no API key and no network, and run against whatever repository
you point them at:

```sh
entire brain bench scale        # index size and query latency vs codebase size
entire brain bench semantic     # indexing throughput and memory
```

Both require a clean worktree — the indexer refuses uncommitted content — and
`--json` emits the full record.

Retrieval quality needs a task set, because a quality number without one is a
number about nothing:

```sh
entire brain facts eval-gen --out tasks.json     # build a task set from this brain
entire brain facts eval --tasks tasks.json       # deterministic when tasks carry labels
entire brain facts eval-compare --a <a.json> --b <b.json>
```

`facts eval` is deterministic and model-free when the task set carries relevance
labels. It calls an agent only if you pass `--judge`, which asks a model to
label relevance instead — that costs tokens, and it is opt-in for exactly that
reason.

## Scale: historical measurements

These September 2026 summaries cover five repositories from 174k to 4.8M lines
on one Apple M-series laptop, using the `syntax-only` profile. They describe the
original benchmark, not the current build. Raw per-query samples and exact
corpus revisions were not retained; these rows cannot be independently
reproduced byte-for-byte.

| Repository | kLOC | Index | KB/kLOC | code search p50 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| entire-api | 174 | 40 MB | 237 | 299 ms |
| entire.io | 485 | 103 MB | 218 | 1,329 ms |
| entiredb | 628 | 112 MB | 183 | 1,407 ms |
| entire-brain | 746 | 193 MB | 265 | 1,315 / 1,945 ms |
| kubernetes | 4,786 | 1,171 MB | 251 | 12,294 ms |

The largest tested repository had a 1,171 MB index and a 12.3-second median
code search. The two entire-brain runs differed by 48%, so read the order of
magnitude rather than the digits. These observations do not establish a scaling
law, a capacity limit, or an advantage over a competitor.

**100M lines has not been measured.** No competitor implementation was run
under this workload. Full method, variance and caveats are in [scale](scale.md).
Re-run the benchmark to evaluate your current build and corpus.

## Retrieval quality: what moved the numbers

These are Brain measured against Brain — one retrieval arm against another on
the same corpus and task set. They are not comparisons with other products.

| Finding | Evidence | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BM25 over substring matching on history | 2.7x–5.1x useful/1k across strata on entire-cli; BM25 gains also observed on two other repositories | BM25 is the no-embedder default |
| EmbeddingGemma fusion over BM25 | +13% useful/1k (t=7.08) and precision +0.016 (t=7.68) at 418k records / 2,584 tasks; replicated at +12.5% (t=5.09) on a second repo | Fused history arm ships, gated on a configured Gemma-class embedder |
| Semantic fusion on facts | +0.459 useful/1k (p=0.005, Holm-significant), precision +0.025, no token cost, n=121 | Fusion default-on for `recall` and `brief` |
| Locus-scoped retrieval | +59% useful/1k (p=0.027 raw, marginal under Holm), −112 tokens (p<0.001), recall −0.029 | Scoped retrieval shipped; outline kept as a map, not a ranker |

Full rows, task sets and corpus identities are in the [eval ledger](eval_ledger.md).

## Agent outcome: one proof-ready result

Retrieval metrics measure retrieval. Whether a brain changes what an agent
*does* is a different question, and a much harder one to answer honestly.

**One measurement has passed our proof gate.** A correctness task whose decided
value exists only in retained history, run five times per side with
`claude:sonnet:high` in the retained August 2026 panel:

| Condition | Validation pass rate |
| --- | ---: |
| no brain | **0 / 5** |
| semantic_history_brain (history channel) | **5 / 5** |

`proof_ready=true` — the lift survives drop-one — with **0 hard integrity flags**
and 20/20 records provenance-backed across the two tasks in the panel. Without the brain the agent cannot recover
the exact decided value; with it, it reads it from history and restores it.

This flipped the history-channel correctness scope from no-claim to claimable.
It is one task on one repository with n=5 per side, scoped to this runner and
history channel. The other task saturated at 5/5 in both arms and is not proof
of lift. The [retained audit](../benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/replay-lab-clean/codex-audit-report.md)
and its manifest are checked by `mise run clean-proof:evidence`. This narrow
result does not establish MCP, Radar, codex-runner, or efficiency agent lift.

## What we deliberately do not claim

Brain's benchmark evidence runs under a **claim policy with an auditor that
refuses citations that have not earned them**. Most retained evidence sits in
`no_release_claim` mode on purpose:

```
claim_policy: no_release_claim
proof_ready_comparisons: 0
```

`mise run release:evidence` fails if a claim-bearing suite is not
provenance-complete, audit-clean, backed by a stable proof-ready comparison, and
run at least four times per side against the *current* task definitions.

So the MCP, Radar, codex-runner and efficiency scopes have numbers, and we do
not cite them. They have not passed the gate. The retained artifacts are kept
specifically so an auditor can see why they are not citable yet.

A clean no-claim audit validates the disclosure; it does not establish an
agent-quality improvement. The separate history-channel lane above has its own
proof-required gate.

## Closed negatives

Things we tried, measured, and dropped. A benchmark page with no losses on it
is a marketing page.

- **Query expansion.** An early d≈0.47 was an n≈8 artifact; at n=121 it
  collapsed to d=0.10, p=0.26. Stays opt-in.
- **Model2Vec fusion on history.** Significantly *worse* than BM25 on precision
  at production scale (t=−6.33 on 418k records, t=−2.84 on a second repo) with
  no useful/1k gain. A promising small-repo +31% was noise.
- **Conversation-exchange fusion.** Traded exact-match precision for one extra
  paraphrase hit. Ships dark behind a flag; `query` stays BM25-only.
- **RRF fusion-weight tuning.** Swept; every cell within noise. Equal weight,
  k0=60 stands.
- **Facts FTS5 BM25 as default.** Parity, not better (1.43 vs 1.50). Opt-in.
- **Scoped-floor via backfill facts.** Dead end.

## Head-to-head against other products

We have not run one.

A defensible head-to-head would need the same corpus, the same task set, the
same judge, and the same token accounting on both sides, with enough repetitions
to survive drop-one — the bar our own claim gate applies. Published numbers from
memory products are generally measured on their own corpora with their own
scorers, so quoting them side by side with ours would compare two different
experiments and call it a comparison.

What we can say from measurement rather than assertion:

- **Historical scale costs are substantial**, as [above](#scale-historical-measurements);
  a comparison against another implementation remains unmeasured.
- **Ingest is deterministic and uses no model**, so indexing cost is wall-clock
  and disk rather than tokens. `bench scale` reports both; there is no API bill
  to compare against.
- **Everything here runs locally**, so you can point our benchmarks at your own
  repository and get your numbers rather than ours.

If you are evaluating Brain against something else, the commands at the top of
this page let you measure your codebase; runtime depends on its size. That is the comparison that
should decide it.

## Method notes

- The scale and retrieval rows are historical summaries, not fresh measurements
  of the current build. The scale source states which reproduction artifacts
  are missing; the eval ledger identifies the retrieval corpora and task sets.
- Results are comparable only within a row's own baseline. Task sets, corpus
  snapshots and metrics differ between rows; the eval ledger states this and it
  applies here too.
- `useful/1k` is useful retrieved content per 1,000 tokens delivered — a
  quality-per-cost measure, so a result can improve precision and still lose on
  it by spending more context.

Runner: `claude:sonnet:high`, five repetitions per side (one above the proof
minimum of four valid rows, because baseline agents on the memory-only task
sometimes escalate to hard adherence violations and forfeit their row).

The fact-merge task regresses a deliberately decided default
(`defaultFactConfidenceThreshold`, the confidence gate for auto-applying a
durable-fact merge/supersede) to a plausible alternative, scrubs the value and
its rationale from everything the agent can read, and only asks it to "restore

- **no_brain (claude:sonnet:high) cannot recover it — 0/5.** It cannot guess the

  so the hidden exact-value check is the sole discriminator.
- **semantic_history_brain retrieves it with the product brain CLI and passes —
  5/5**, with >=20% improvements in both time-or-tokens and search-call volume.

This is a stable `brain_positive` comparison (pass-rate lift surviving the
drop-one robustness check), so `proof_ready=true`.

## Isolation — why a brain win can only come from retrieval

Every cell runs under the same physical isolation:

- a deny-first `sandbox-exec` profile: harness and source trees unreadable,

  caches re-allowed;

- the brain store republished through the product after sanitization, so the
  treatment loads a coherent index built over exactly the scrubbed bytes.

Brain is live and healthy here: version 0.1.0, 411 distilled facts, index current at HEAD, one cosmetic warning that the fact manifest is behind the store (`entire brain refresh` clears it). I used it to answer your question rather than guessing.

**The demo: "the regression only memory can fix."** It's the one result Entire has actually earned the right to claim, and I verified the key moment works on your machine just now.

The spine comes straight from the retained evidence. In the August proof panel, an agent was asked to restore a deliberately decided default that had been changed to a plausible alternative, with the rationale scrubbed from everything it could read. Without Brain, Claude Sonnet got 0 of 5. With Brain's history channel, 5 of 5. That is the only agent-outcome claim that passed the project's own proof gate, and the audit has zero integrity flags. Everything else (MCP, Radar, efficiency) is explicitly no-claim.

How I'd stage it, about five minutes:

1. **The question the code can't answer.** Open `defaultFactConfidenceThreshold = 0.75`. Ask the room: why 0.75? grep finds nothing, blame gives a commit that says "set threshold". Every codebase has a hundred of these.
2. **Agent without memory.** Flip it to 0.7, ask a plain Claude Code session to "restore the intended default from project history". Tests pass at 0.7, 0.75 and 0.8, so it guesses. Safe to run live given the 0 of 5.
3. **Same agent, Brain on.** The first fact back from recall on this exact question is the decision: cross-member conflicts default to keep-both plus review, merge or supersede gated at confidence 0.75. It also surfaces a second fact that is pure gold: an earlier run of this very benchmark was confounded because git history leaked the answer. Memory about memory. The audience sees *why*, not just *what*.
4. **Receipts.** Show the benchmarks page: 0 of 5 vs 5 of 5, the proof gate, and the closed-negatives section. "A benchmark page with no losses is a marketing page" is the line that separates this from every other memory product.
5. **The close.** `entire brain brief "<their task>"` on the prospect's own repo. No API key, no network, deterministic ingest. The demo becomes an on-site pilot in the same meeting.

**One real hazard, caught by Brain itself.** That leakage fact applies to your live demo too: in an un-scrubbed clone, git log exposes 0.75 and the no-brain agent might find it. Either reuse the harness's scrubbed-clone setup (it already does binary replacement and history scrubbing) or pick a decision whose value never appears in a commit message. Also, a prior doc note warns that a demo on the legacy checkpoint branch layout isn't what a new user gets, so stage it on a freshly enabled repo.

What I'd skip: the progress-bar setup scripts (they demo rendering, not value) and the scale table (historical, not reproducible, and the doc says so).

Two tool notes for the record: `recall --evidence` failed here with "ambiguous session identity in evidence branch", so plain recall is the reliable live command. Recall takes `--k`, not `--limit`.

I can turn this into a reproducible demo repo with the scrubbed clone and a run script if you want it for the next customer call.
But this will work with sessions as well right? how is brain adding value here?

Fair challenge, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a defence. Let me check what the baseline in that proof actually had, and whether any retained evidence compares Brain against plain session search.

content.text:
You're right to push on this, and the honest answer is that the proof-ready result does not show it.

**What the 0/5 vs 5/5 actually proves.** The baseline in that panel had no sessions at all. The record flags say agent-visible Entire history was removed and checkpoint objects were repacked away and verified gone. So the comparison is memory versus no memory, not Brain versus raw session search. There is no retained evidence comparing Brain against an agent armed with `entire search` or checkpoint transcripts. A sharp customer would ask exactly what you just asked, and the demo as I framed it walks into that.

**Where Brain actually adds value over sessions**, split by what's measured and what's reasoning:

Measured, Brain against its own weaker arms on the same corpus:
- BM25 ranking over history beat substring matching by 2.7x to 5.1x useful content per thousand tokens. That is the closest thing to "Brain vs naive session search" in the ledger.
- Locus-scoped retrieval cut tokens per answer. Fact fusion improved precision at no token cost.

First principles, what a transcript cannot give you:
- **Verdict, not mention.** The session hit for the threshold lands at line 4096 of a transcript, amid grep commands trying 0.7, 0.75 and 0.8. The agent still has to read the session to learn which value was decided versus merely tried. The fact says it in one sentence, typed as a decision, with confidence and branch.
- **Negative knowledge.** The strongest facts in this store are closed-negatives: "tried, measured, dropped, revisit only if". Session search surfaces the attempt. Nothing in a transcript says it was abandoned. That knowledge is synthesized across sessions and is the thing new engineers and agents get wrong most.
- **Staleness.** Facts anchor to source and `verify` reports stale or orphaned ones. A transcript cannot tell you it's out of date.
- **Task-shaped assembly.** Brief returns facts, history, semantic neighbours, likely edit and test files in one call. Session search is a query you must already know to ask.
- **Local and offline.** Entire search needs login and the hosted search service. Brain runs with no network, no model and no egress. For enterprise or air-gapped teams that is the whole conversation.

**What this changes about the demo.** Drop "find the number". Change the question to "should we lower the merge gate to 0.7?" Brain answers with the decision, the rationale, and the gotcha that an earlier benchmark at 0.7 was confounded by answer leakage. Session search gives you forty hits to read. That is the contrast worth showing.

**What I'd do before any customer sees it.** Run the head-to-head yourself: plain Claude Code with `entire search --compact` versus Brain, same prompt, three reps each. The harness already supports named conditions, so a sessions-only arm is a day's work, and you then have the number to say out loud instead of a theory. If sessions-only also passes, that is important to know now, not on a call.

# Coordinated agent instructions

Both products provide `init-agents` and `agent-guide`, invoked through
`entire graph` and `entire brain`. Brain also retains `guide` as an alias.

## Repository activation

Each `init-agents` enables only the invoking product and preserves products already
enabled in this repository. Running Graph and Brain initializers in either order
produces the same combined guide. Installing a plugin globally, creating Brain
runtime setup, or building an index does not activate its agent guidance.
Generation does not query the host inventory or invoke another plugin.

The shared guide contains a versioned machine-readable comment:

```html
<!-- entire-agent-activation: {"schema_version":1,"enabled":["graph","brain"]} -->
```

This record is authoritative. The renderer adds the invoking product, orders the
enabled list as Graph then Brain, and regenerates the guide and record together
through the existing atomic file replacement. Malformed metadata, unknown
products, and unsupported versions fail before writes. There is no separate
activation file that can diverge from the installed guide.

For guides without metadata, migration preserves the products represented by
recognized generated guide headings and validated legacy managed blocks. Legacy
redirects do not independently activate anything. Existing combined guidance
remains combined: old output cannot distinguish explicit activation from a peer
inferred by earlier versions. Unrecognized guides fail without being overwritten.
Once metadata exists, stale legacy instructions cannot override it.

## Preview and lifecycle

`agent-guide` remains read-only: it previews adding the invoking product to the
repository activation without persisting that addition. Outside a repository it
prints the standalone reference without activation metadata.

Runtime data deletion, plugin removal, and temporary tool unavailability do not
remove repository activation. To explicitly remove a product, remove its name
from the metadata's enabled list, then regenerate using a remaining enabled
product. To remove all activation, remove the guide and managed instruction
pointers (and any legacy redirects). There is no new removal command.

Both binaries must be upgraded to this contract. Older binaries can overwrite
the metadata or infer activation using their old rules.

## Guidance mode

Both commands accept mutually exclusive `--strict` and `--normal` flags.
`init-agents --strict` persists strict guidance for every enabled product in this
repository. Subsequent initialization and previews inherit that mode, including
when the other product is added. `init-agents --normal` persistently resets it.
New repositories and legacy guides default to normal.

`agent-guide` is always read-only. Its `--strict` and `--normal` flags override
only the current preview; they never change the repository's saved mode. Outside
a repository it prints the selected standalone guide, defaulting to normal.

Strict guidance requires Graph for structural questions and impact analysis before

content.text:
I ran it. The result is not the one you'd want on stage, and it's more useful than a win.

**The question everyone can follow.** "A teammate proposes: when you install the Entire plugins globally, Brain should switch on automatically in every repo. Should we? Has this been decided before?" The recorded answer exists only in agent sessions: on 16 September Thomas called a change that did exactly this "a regression" and said "Installing Brain globally should never enable it in a repo." The commit message says nothing, the docs state the rule but not the reason, and Brain holds it as a closed-negative fact.

**Setup.** Fresh clone per run, Claude Code headless on Sonnet, read-only tools, same prompt. A shim on PATH gates which `entire` subcommands exist per condition. Each condition got the product's own generated guide. Three repetitions each.

| Condition | Recovered the recorded rejection | Mean time | Mean cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Code and git only | 0 of 3, all honestly said "inferred" | 32 s | $0.20 |
| 2. Plus sessions (hosted search and explain) | **3 of 3**, quoted it verbatim | 32 s | $0.17 |
| 3. Plus Graph | 0 of 3, one partial | 61 s | $0.21 |
| 4. Plus Brain, normal guide | 0 of 3, two partial | 42 s | $0.19 |
| 5. Plus Brain, strict guide | 1 of 3 | 213 s | $0.32 |

**Why Brain lost to plain sessions.** Not retrieval. Brain had the exact fact and the exact session line in the brief on every run. Two product defects stopped the agent from seeing them.

# The nested agent runs read-only: explicit tool allowlist, no permission bypass, no session persistence.
# Graph prewarm (conditions 3+) is excluded from timing and written to prewarm.txt.
set -eu
COND=$1; REP=$2; Q=${3:-global-activation}
here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
SRC=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
OUT=${LADDER_OUT:-$here/runs}
ORIGIN=${LADDER_ORIGIN:-$(git -C "$SRC" remote get-url origin)}
RUN=$OUT/$Q/c${COND}-r${REP}
[ -f "$here/guides/cond${COND}.md" ] || { echo "guides missing; run setup-guides.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$here/questions/$Q.txt" ] || { echo "unknown question $Q" >&2; exit 1; }
rm -rf "$RUN"; mkdir -p "$RUN"
git clone -q "$SRC" "$RUN/repo"
cd "$RUN/repo"
git remote set-url origin "$ORIGIN"
cp "$here/guides/cond${COND}.md" CLAUDE.md
rm -f .entire/agent-guide.md
[ "$COND" = 1 ] && rm -f .claude/agents/entire-search.md
export PATH="$here/bin:$PATH" LADDER_COND=$COND
if [ "$COND" -ge 3 ]; then
  s=$(date +%s); entire graph index --repo . --profile full >"$RUN/prewarm.log" 2>&1 || true
  echo "prewarm_s=$(( $(date +%s) - s ))" > "$RUN/prewarm.txt"
fi
ALLOW="Read Grep Glob Agent Bash(git:*) Bash(entire:*) Bash(grep:*) Bash(rg:*) Bash(ls:*) Bash(cat:*) Bash(head:*) Bash(tail:*) Bash(sed -n:*) Bash(find:*) Bash(wc:*) Bash(go doc:*)"
start=$(date +%s)
claude -p "$(cat "$here/questions/$Q.txt")" --model "${LADDER_MODEL:-sonnet}" --output-format stream-json --verbose \
  --setting-sources project --no-session-persistence --max-turns "${LADDER_MAX_TURNS:-80}" \
  --allowedTools $ALLOW --disallowedTools "Edit Write MultiEdit NotebookEdit WebFetch WebSearch" \
  > "$RUN/stream.jsonl" 2> "$RUN/stderr.log" || echo "exit=$?" > "$RUN/failed.txt"
echo "wall_s=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))" > "$RUN/wall.txt"
python3 "$here/parse.py" "$RUN" > "$RUN/summary.json"
echo "done $Q c${COND}-r${REP}"
EOF
cat > $D/run-all.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Run every condition sequentially for N repetitions (arms are not run in parallel so they do not
# contend for the hosted search service, the Brain store or the Graph cache).
#   run-all.sh [reps=3] [question=global-activation] [conditions="1 2 3 4 5"]
set -eu
here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
REPS=${1:-3}; Q=${2:-global-activation}; CONDS=${3:-"1 2 3 4 5"}
sh "$here/setup-guides.sh"
r=1
while [ "$r" -le "$REPS" ]; do
  for c in $CONDS; do sh "$here/run.sh" "$c" "$r" "$Q"; done
  r=$((r + 1))
done
python3 "$here/grade.py" "$Q"
EOF
chmod +x $D/setup-guides.sh $D/run.sh $D/run-all.sh
printf 'runs/\nguides/\n' > $D/.gitignore

cat > benchmarks/memory-ladder/README.md <<'EOF'
# Memory ladder

A small, reproducible comparison of what a coding agent can answer about a
repository's past as you add memory surfaces one step at a time:

| Cond | Agent has | Guide the agent receives |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | source tree and git history | plain note; no Entire tooling |
| 2 | + hosted session history (`entire search`, `entire checkpoint explain --full`) | plain note + session section |
| 3 | + Graph (`entire graph query`, `neighbors`, `impact`) | `entire graph agent-guide` rendered outside a repository (standalone Graph) + session section |
| 4 | + Brain, normal guidance | `entire graph agent-guide` rendered inside this repository (combined Graph and Brain) + session section |
| 5 | + Brain, strict guidance | this repository's committed `.entire/agent-guide.md` + session section |

Every condition runs the same prompt against a fresh clone with the same
read-only tool allowlist. A shim first on `PATH` decides which `entire`
subcommands exist, so an agent cannot reach a surface its condition excludes,
and lifecycle hooks are swallowed so nested runs never capture checkpoints. The
guides are generated from the product at run time, not checked in.

The question is the kind a product manager asks, not an engineer: "should we
auto-activate Brain on global install, and was this decided before?" Its
recorded answer exists only in agent session history and as a Brain
closed-negative fact, not in code, docs or commit messages.

## Run it

Requirements: `claude` (Claude Code CLI), `entire` logged in (hosted search needs
it), `entire graph` and `entire brain` plugins installed, a clean checkout.

```sh
benchmarks/memory-ladder/run-all.sh            # 3 reps x 5 conditions, sequential, then grade
benchmarks/memory-ladder/run.sh 2 1            # one condition, one rep
python3 benchmarks/memory-ladder/grade.py      # table of runs and per-condition means
```

Knobs: `LADDER_MODEL` (default `sonnet`), `LADDER_MAX_TURNS` (80), `LADDER_OUT`
(default `runs/`, gitignored), `LADDER_ORIGIN` (clone origin URL; Brain and
Graph derive the repository key from it, so keep the GitHub URL). Graph prewarm
for conditions 3 and above is excluded from timing and recorded in `prewarm.txt`.

Each run leaves `stream.jsonl` (the full agent transcript), `summary.json`
(metrics, every shell command, the final answer) and the clone it ran in.
Add a question by dropping `questions/<name>.txt` and
`questions/<name>.rubric.json`; the rubric is named regexes over the final answer
and its `recovered` key is a first pass that should be hand-checked.

## What the first run found (2026-10-06)

Three repetitions per condition, Sonnet, this repository at `main`. "Recovered"
means the answer stated the recorded decision and its reason, not an inference
from the resulting rule.

| Cond | Recovered | Mean input tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 code + git | 0/3 | 303k |
| 2 + sessions | 3/3 | 203k |
| 3 + Graph | 0/3 (1 partial) | 224k |
| 4 + Brain, normal | 0/3 (2 partial) | 219k |
| 5 + Brain, strict | 1/3 | 487k |

Brain retrieved the decisive fact and the decisive session line in the brief on
every run. The agent did not see them: `brief --json` leads with a ~12.8 KB
status block and puts `facts` and `history` last, and every agent capped the
output before reaching them. `query` returned only `doc` results for natural
phrasings while `recall` ranked the fact first. Tracked in
[#335](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/issues/335). Re-run this ladder
after that fix before claiming Brain lift over plain session access.

## Caveats

- One question, one repository, one model, n=3. Treat it as a probe, not a
  benchmark; the claim gate in `docs/benchmarks.md` does not apply to it.
- Conditions 2 to 5 depend on the hosted search service, so results vary with
  what has been synced. Condition 1 has no network surface.
- The first run executed arms in parallel; `run-all.sh` runs them sequentially
  per the recorded benchmark convention. Re-check timing before quoting it.
EOF
echo README_OK

## What

`benchmarks/memory-ladder/`: a small reproducible harness that asks one plain-language question about the repository's past under five conditions, adding a memory surface each step: code and git only; + hosted sessions; + Graph; + Brain with the normal generated guide; + Brain with the strict guide.

- `run.sh` clones the repo fresh, sets the condition's guide as `CLAUDE.md`, and runs Claude Code headless with a read-only tool allowlist and no permission bypass.
- `bin/entire` is a PATH shim that gates `entire` subcommands per condition and swallows lifecycle hooks so nested runs never capture checkpoints.
- `setup-guides.sh` renders the guides from `entire graph agent-guide` and the committed `.entire/agent-guide.md` at run time, so nothing checked in goes stale.
- `run-all.sh` runs arms sequentially (per the recorded benchmark convention); Graph prewarm is excluded from timing.
- `parse.py` / `grade.py` turn `stream-json` transcripts into metrics, the full command list, the final answer, and rubric hits. Rubrics are per-question regex files; `recovered` is a first pass meant to be hand-checked.

## Why

The published proof-ready result compares memory against no memory. This probe compares Brain against an agent that already has plain session access, which is the question a customer asks. The first run (n=3, Sonnet) recovered the recorded decision 0/3, 3/3, 0/3, 0/3, 1/3 across the five conditions. Brain retrieved the decisive fact and session line in the brief every time; agents truncated `brief --json` before reaching them because a ~12.8 KB status block comes first, and `query` returned only docs for natural phrasings. Filed as #335. The README records the result with input tokens only and says to re-run after the fix before claiming lift.

## Scope

Adds one directory. No Go or Python code under `internal/` or `benchmarks/agent-brain/` changes. `runs/` and `guides/` are gitignored. Not wired into mise or CI; it costs real agent tokens and needs a logged-in `entire`.

## Verified

- `sh -n` on all scripts, `py_compile` on both Python files.
- `setup-guides.sh` renders all five guides on this machine.
- Shim gating checked for conditions 1, 2 and 3.
- End-to-end smoke of `run.sh 2 1` from the checked-in path, then `grade.py` over its output.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

BODY: `REAL=${LADDER_REAL_ENTIRE:-$(command -v -p entire 2>/dev/null || echo /opt/homebrew/bin/entire)}` uses `command -v -p`, which per POSIX searches a system-default PATH guaranteed only to find standard utilities, not a third-party CLI like `entire` installed outside that default set (e.g. via npm/go install/curl installer to `~/.local/bin`). content.text:
Done. Trail 251 is clean: the third review pass ran on commit be8ddbcf and produced no comments, and the findings gate passed.

What was resolved, across two rounds:

- **High: the clone shipped its own answer key.** The runner now removes the harness directory from the clone's worktree and HEAD tree before the agent starts, and clones `main` explicitly because Brain scopes facts per branch. I checked that the extra commit only changes Brain's freshness label and leaves facts and history intact.
- **Medium: shim resolved the real CLI through a Homebrew fallback.** It now resolves from PATH minus its own directory and fails with an explicit message if nothing is found.
- **Medium: grader averaged failed runs.** Completion is recorded per run, means and the recovered denominator use completed runs only, and failed runs are listed separately.
- **Medium and low, second pass: unvalidated path inputs.** The question name is checked against a safe pattern in both the grader and the runner before it reaches a path or an `rm -rf`, and the parser accepts only an existing run directory.

Each fix was verified with a rejection test and a happy-path run before being pushed, and each finding was resolved with the commit hash and what was checked. The PR is at https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/336 with three commits. CI checks are still in progress on the latest head, and the trail has no approvals yet, so merge is waiting on a human reviewer.
next up?

Fix #335, then re-run the ladder. That's the one move that turns today's loss into the demo you asked for this morning, and it's small.

**1. Fix the two defects in Brain.** Reorder the JSON brief so facts, history and likely files come before status, with full status behind a flag. Have the generated guides name `recall "<question>"` as the first call for prior-decision questions, and make `query` return facts for natural phrasings or stop pointing agents at it. Both changes sit in `internal/cli` and the guide templates; impact analysis first since brief's JSON shape has test contracts. Half a day including tests.

**2. Re-run the ladder against the fix.** Same five conditions, three reps, about ten minutes and two dollars. One caveat the harness README already flags: today's sessions discuss the answer and are now in hosted history and will be distilled into the brain, so condition 2 and up can find them. Either exclude those sessions or write a second question whose answer hasn't been discussed. I'd write the second question; it also shows the result isn't a one-off.

**3. If Brain then wins on tokens and time while matching sessions on recovery,** that is the demo: five terminals, one plain question, a ladder of answers, with numbers that survive a sharp audience because the losing run is on the same page.

In parallel, PR #336 needs a human approval on the trail, and the memory note about Graph's `query` command is already corrected. I'd start on the brief reorder now unless you'd rather I write the second question first.
Let's go

## What

Two of the three fixes proposed in #335.

**1. `brief --json` emits the retrieval payload first and status last.** The key order of `brainBriefJSONReport` is now `generated_at, task, facts (+ fact annotations), history, conversation, likely_edit_files, likely_test_files, likely_files, action_checklist, guidance, warnings, semantic, status`. Nothing is added or removed; only the order changes. The MCP `brain_brief` tool shares this projection, so it changes too.

Measured on this repository for the question in #335: the decisive fact moved from after byte ~17,000 to byte 315, and `status` (mostly provider freshness warnings) now starts at byte ~10,800 instead of byte 135. An agent that caps a tool result at 6 KB now sees the facts and history sections.

**2. Both generated guides name `recall` for prior-decision questions.** The normal guide (`brainWorkflow`) gets a paragraph after the brief command: questions about why, what was decided, or what was tried are answered by durable facts; retrieve with `entire brain recall "<question>" --json`; the brief's facts section is a sample and `query` can rank documentation above the recorded decision. The strict guide gets the same as a directive. Pinned phrases from the existing coordination tests are untouched.

`.entire/agent-guide.md` in this repository is regenerated with the new binary (strict mode is inherited). The diff also picks up the `remember` paragraph that the shipped text already had and the committed guide did not.

## Not in this PR

- `query` ranking. In hybrid mode docs contribute two RRF lists (lexical and vector) while facts contribute one fused list, so docs get double mass; `--keyword` returns a balanced 4 doc / 3 fact / 3 history for the same question with the fact at rank 2. Changing fusion is retrieval-quality work that the recorded convention says needs the eval pack regenerated and a ledger entry first. Noted on #335.
- The Graph mirror of `internal/agentsetup`. Graph's `main` already diverges from Brain's `guide.go` (Graph restored directive normal-mode wording on its side, with a recorded rationale in its file header; Brain's copy and its tests still carry the softened phrases). The parity script only runs when a local Graph checkout exists and is not in CI. A matching Graph change should follow, but reconciling the two guides is a separate decision.

## Verified

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/cli`, `gofmt -l` clean.
- `go test ./internal/agentsetup` passes, including the new `TestBrainGuidesNameRecallForPriorDecisions` (recall text present in brain and combined guides in both modes, absent from Graph-only guides, and placed after the brief command).

D=benchmarks/memory-ladder && cat > $D/bin/git <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Read-only, harness-blind git for the agent under test. run.sh puts this directory first on PATH.
#
# Why: the harness directory (prompt, rubric, README with earlier results) is stripped from the
# clone's worktree and HEAD, but once it has merged it still exists in history, and the agent's
# tool allowlist permits git. This wrapper keeps git history available as a memory surface
# (condition 1 depends on it) while closing every read path to that directory:
#   - only read subcommands are allowed (no fetch/pull, no object-level readers, no writes);
#   - any argument that names the directory or a rubric is refused;
#   - for history and content readers a pathspec exclusion is appended, so `git show <sha>` and
#     `git log -p` cannot print the directory even for the commits that added it.
# The transcript audit in parse.py records refused attempts; see README.
HARNESS=benchmarks/memory-ladder
shimdir=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
PATH=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -vx -- "$shimdir" | paste -sd: -); export PATH
REAL=$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$REAL" ] || { echo "git shim: real git not found on PATH" >&2; exit 127; }
sub=${1:-}
deny() { echo "git: $1 is not available in this environment" >&2; exit 1; }
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in *memory-ladder*|*memory_ladder*|*rubric*) deny "that path" ;; esac
done
case "$sub" in
  log|show|diff|whatchanged|range-diff|shortlog|grep|blame|annotate)
    has_sep=0; for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = "--" ] && has_sep=1; done
    case "$sub" in
      blame|annotate) exec "$REAL" "$@" ;;   # single-file readers: the path itself is already screened above
      *) if [ "$has_sep" = 1 ]; then exec "$REAL" "$@" ":!$HARNESS"; else exec "$REAL" "$@" -- ":!$HARNESS"; fi ;;
    esac ;;
  status|branch|tag|describe|rev-parse|name-rev|merge-base|ls-files|for-each-ref|show-branch|show-ref|help|version|--version|config)
    case "$sub$2" in config*) case "$2" in --get|--list|-l|--get-all|--get-regexp) ;; *) deny "git config writes" ;; esac ;; esac
    exec "$REAL" "$@" ;;
  *) deny "git $sub" ;;
esac
EOF
chmod +x $D/bin/git
python3 - <<'EOF'
D="benchmarks/memory-ladder"
p=f"{D}/parse.py"; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''tools = collections.Counter(); cmds = []; result = {}''','''tools = collections.Counter(); cmds = []; result = {}
# Leakage audit: the harness directory is stripped from the clone, but an agent may still probe
# for it. Probes are recorded; a tool result that carries rubric or README content marks the run
# contaminated so grade.py excludes it.
HARNESS_MARKERS = ("memory-ladder", "memory_ladder", "rubric")
CONTENT_MARKERS = ('"recovered"', ".rubric.json", "_comment", "## Run 1", "## Run 2", "Recovered the recorded")
probes = []; contaminated = False''')
s=s.replace('''                if b["name"] == "Bash":
                    cmds.append(b["input"].get("command", "")[:300])''','''                if b["name"] == "Bash":
                    cmds.append(b["input"].get("command", "")[:300])
                probe_text = json.dumps(b.get("input", {}))
                if any(m in probe_text for m in HARNESS_MARKERS):
                    probes.append(b["name"] + ": " + probe_text[:200])''')
s=s.replace('''    elif ev.get("type") == "result":
        result = ev''','''    elif ev.get("type") == "user":
        for b in ev.get("message", {}).get("content", []):
            if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                body = b.get("content"); body = body if isinstance(body, str) else json.dumps(body)
                if any(m in body for m in CONTENT_MARKERS) and "not available in this environment" not in body:
                    contaminated = True
    elif ev.get("type") == "result":
        result = ev''')
s=s.replace('''    "completed": completed, "failed_marker": failed_marker,''','''    "completed": completed, "failed_marker": failed_marker,
    "harness_probes": probes, "contaminated": contaminated,''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
p=f"{D}/grade.py"; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    if not completed:
        hits = {k: None for k in rubric}  # an unfinished run has no answer to grade''','''    if d.get("contaminated"):
        completed = False  # the agent saw harness content; its answer cannot be graded
    if not completed:
        hits = {k: None for k in rubric}  # an unfinished or contaminated run has no answer to grade''')
s=s.replace('''    rows.append({"run": d["cond"], "completed": completed, **{k: d.get(k) for k in ("duration_s", "cost_usd", "num_turns", "tool_calls", "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "is_error", "subtype", "entire_subcommands")}, **hits})''','''    rows.append({"run": d["cond"], "completed": completed, "contaminated": bool(d.get("contaminated")), "probes": len(d.get("harness_probes") or []), **{k: d.get(k) for k in ("duration_s", "cost_usd", "num_turns", "tool_calls", "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "is_error", "subtype", "entire_subcommands")}, **hits})''')
s=s.replace('''failed = [r["run"] for r in rows if not r["completed"]]
if failed:
    print("\\nfailed or incomplete runs (excluded from means):", ", ".join(failed))''','''failed = [r["run"] for r in rows if not r["completed"] and not r["contaminated"]]
if failed:
    print("\\nfailed or incomplete runs (excluded from means):", ", ".join(failed))
bad = [r["run"] for r in rows if r["contaminated"]]
if bad:
    print("contaminated runs, agent saw harness content (excluded):", ", ".join(bad))
probed = [f'{r["run"]}({r["probes"]})' for r in rows if r["probes"]]
if probed:
    print("runs that probed for the harness directory (refused, kept):", ", ".join(probed))''')
open(p,"w").write(s); print("patched")
